title: North Island vs South Island for Families — Which to Choose First?
meta_desc: Discover which NZ island is best for families, considering activity density, drive times, ages, cost difference, and what you'll miss if you only visit one island
intro: When planning a family trip to New Zealand, one of the toughest decisions is choosing between the North and South Islands. With so many amazing attractions and activities on both islands, it can be overwhelming to decide which one to visit first. The North Island offers a plethora of urban attractions, such as Auckland's Sky Tower and Wellington's Te Papa Museum, while the South Island boasts breathtaking natural landscapes like Milford Sound and Franz Josef Glacier.

sections.heading: Activity Density
sections.body: The North Island has a higher activity density, with many popular attractions like the Bay of Islands, Rotorua, and Taupo, all within a few hours' drive from Auckland. In contrast, the South Island's activities are more spread out, requiring longer drive times between destinations. For example, driving from Queenstown to Milford Sound takes around 4 hours, while driving from Auckland to Rotorua takes around 2.5 hours.

sections.heading: Age-Specific Activities
list: For young children (0-5 years): The North Island's Auckland Zoo ($25 per adult, $13 per child) and Kelly Tarlton's Sea Life Aquarium ($39 per adult, $25 per child) are great options.
For older kids (6-12 years): The South Island's Queenstown has many adventure activities like skydiving ($299 per person) and bungee jumping ($205 per person).
For teenagers (13+ years): The North Island's surf beaches, such as Raglan and Piha, offer great surf lessons ($50-$70 per person) and a relaxed atmosphere.

sections.heading: Cost Difference
sections.body: Accommodation prices vary significantly between the two islands. On average, a family-friendly motel in the North Island costs around $150-$250 per night, while in the South Island, it costs around $120-$200 per night. Activity prices also differ, with the South Island's adventure activities often costing more than the North Island's urban attractions. For example, a family pass to the Sky Tower in Auckland costs $99, while a scenic flight over Milford Sound costs $395 per person.

sections.heading: What You'll Miss
sections.body: If you only visit the North Island, you'll miss the stunning natural beauty of the South Island, including Milford Sound, Franz Josef Glacier, and Abel Tasman National Park. On the other hand, if you only visit the South Island, you'll miss the urban attractions and cultural experiences of the North Island, such as Auckland's city life, Rotorua's geothermal wonders, and Wellington's Te Papa Museum.
